symbols.w: the weight vector: how much each feature counts; it sets the direction of the boundary
symbols.bf:x: one example as a whole vector of feature values
symbols.x: one example, or a single feature value of it (the slides are loose about bold)
symbols.i: counts training examples, from 1 to m
symbols.alpha: the weight on training example i: a multiplier in the SVM, a mistake count in the perceptron
symbols.t: the threshold: the boundary is w dot x = t, so the bias b equals minus t
symbols.y: the true label of a training example, +1 or -1
symbols.C: the price of breaking the margin in the soft margin SVM: high C punishes violations hard
symbols.norm: the length of a vector (subscript 2: straight-line length; subscript 1: sum of absolute values)
symbols.sum: add up the term that follows, once for every value of the index shown
symbols.j: counts training examples, a second index so pairs of examples can be summed
symbols.z: the margin of an example: score times true label, positive if right and negative if wrong
symbols.K: the kernel: a function giving the dot product of two examples in the new feature space
symbols.xi: the slack of example i: how far it falls short of the required score of 1
symbols.c: the constant added inside the polynomial kernel, which brings in the lower-order terms
symbols.L: a loss: the penalty charged for an example's margin
symbols.d: the number of features (dimensions) of an example
symbols.p: the power (order) of a polynomial: how many factors multiply in each new feature
symbols.s: marks the closest point to the boundary, written as x with subscript s
symbols.T: transpose: turns a column vector into a row so the product is a dot product
symbols.abs: absolute value of a number; for a set, how many items it contains
symbols.g: a constraint function: the constraint is satisfied when g is zero or negative
symbols.f: the classifier's decision function: gives +1 or -1 for an example
symbols.b: the bias: the constant added to the weighted sum of features
symbols.varphi: the feature map: turns an example into a longer vector of new features
symbols.cal:L: the Lagrangian: the objective plus a fine for every constraint
symbols.exp: the exponential function: e raised to the power that follows
symbols.G: the Gram matrix: a table of dot products between every pair of examples
symbols.cal:Z: the new feature space that the feature map sends examples into
symbols.X: the data matrix with one row per training example
symbols.sigma: the width of the RBF (Gaussian) kernel: how far apart points can be and still count as similar
symbols.phi: the feature map (tutorial notation): turns an example into a vector of new features
symbols.hat:y: the predicted label: the sign of the weighted sum
symbols.r: the radius of the circle that separates the classes
symbols.max: the largest value of what follows
symbols.min: the smallest value of what follows
symbols.beta: the multiplier that enforces slack being non-negative in the soft margin SVM
symbols.bf:y: a second data point (not a label), in the tutorial's kernel questions
symbols.q: the power of the polynomial kernel in the slides
symbols.hat:s: the classifier's score for an example: how strongly it favours the positive class
symbols.in: is an element of, belongs to
symbols.w:sign: the sign function: +1 if the value is positive, -1 if negative
symbols.cal:Y: the output space: the set of values the model can return
symbols.cal:X: the input space: the set of all possible examples
symbols.bf:z: an example after the feature map: a vector in the new feature space
symbols.h: marks the hinge loss, as in the subscript of the hinge loss L
symbols.w:sgn: the sign function: +1 if the value is positive, -1 otherwise
symbols.w:subject to: the rule that must hold while the quantity before it is optimised
symbols.arg: the value of the unknowns that makes what follows as large (arg max) or small (arg min) as possible
symbols.D: the training set; its size is the number of training examples
symbols.lambda: the regularisation weight from earlier units, which works in the opposite direction to C
symbols.hat:c: the learned classifier: maps an example to a class
symbols.hat:S: the scoring classifier: maps an example to one score per class
symbols.w:if: the condition under which this case applies
symbols.partial: partial derivative: the slope with respect to one variable, others held fixed
symbols.nabla: the gradient: the slopes with respect to every weight, taken together
symbols.w:sv: the set of support vectors: the examples with non-zero multiplier
symbols.w:for any support vector: the formula holds if you plug in any one support vector
symbols.gamma: a smaller feature map that also separates XOR

The big picture.p: the tutorial's number of features; in the slides' p.35 polynomial kernel, the degree
The big picture.k: the tutorial's name for the kernel function (the slides write K)

When a linear classifier.n: the order of the new features: how many factors multiply in each term
When a linear classifier.p: the order: how many factors multiply in each new feature
When a linear classifier.x: an original attribute value, such as x_1 or x_2
When a linear classifier.w: a weight on one of the new product features

The perceptron in dual form.alpha: the number of mistakes made on example i, used as its weight
The perceptron in dual form.j: counts training examples, so each pair can be compared
The perceptron in dual form.G: the Gram matrix of dot products between all pairs of examples
The perceptron in dual form.X: the data matrix with one row per example
The perceptron in dual form.w: the weight vector, built as a sum of signed examples

The kernel trick.x: one example, or one of its feature values
The kernel trick.z: an example after the feature map: a point in the new space
The kernel trick.bf:z: an example after the feature map: a point in the new space
The kernel trick.d: the degree of the polynomial kernel in the tutorial's notation
The kernel trick.k: the tutorial's name for the kernel function
The kernel trick.K: the kernel: the new-space dot product, computed from the original examples
The kernel trick.c: the constant added inside the polynomial kernel
The kernel trick.q: the power of the polynomial kernel
The kernel trick.b: the scale of the Laplace kernel: bigger b means a gentler fall-off
The kernel trick.sigma: the RBF width: bigger sigma makes distant pairs still score near 1
The kernel trick.alpha: how many mistakes were made on example i: its vote strength
The kernel trick.hat:y: the predicted label: the sign of the weighted vote of training examples

The support vector machine: geometry.m: the scaled margin in the lines w dot x = t plus or minus m; in i = 1 to m, the example count
The support vector machine: geometry.w: the weight vector: perpendicular to the boundary, with no bias inside it
The support vector machine: geometry.t: the threshold: the boundary is w dot x = t
The support vector machine: geometry.s: marks the closest point to the boundary, x_s
The support vector machine: geometry.abs: absolute value: the size of the score, ignoring its sign
The support vector machine: geometry.norm: the length of w: a shorter w means a wider margin
The support vector machine: geometry.min: the smallest value of what follows, trying the unknowns (or examples) written underneath
The support vector machine: geometry.max: the largest value, here the widest margin
The support vector machine: geometry.w:subject to: the rule that must hold: every example clears its margin

Lagrange multipliers.x: a variable of the function being minimised, in the general method
Lagrange multipliers.g: a constraint function: the constraint holds when g is zero or below
Lagrange multipliers.j: counts the constraints in the general method; later, training examples
Lagrange multipliers.alpha: the multiplier (fine rate) for one constraint; for the SVM, one per example
Lagrange multipliers.cal:L: the Lagrangian: the objective plus a fine for every constraint
Lagrange multipliers.t: the threshold of the boundary, a quantity to minimise over
Lagrange multipliers.G: the labelled Gram matrix: pairwise dot products with the label signs included
Lagrange multipliers.X: the labelled data matrix whose rows are the label times each example
Lagrange multipliers.partial: partial derivative: the slope with respect to the one variable shown
Lagrange multipliers.nabla: the gradient with respect to w: its slopes for every weight at once
Lagrange multipliers.T: transpose, as in the row y_i x_i^T
Lagrange multipliers.f: the objective function being minimised, in the general method
Lagrange multipliers.n: the number of variables in the general method; elsewhere the number of features
Lagrange multipliers.max: the largest value, taken over the multipliers
Lagrange multipliers.min: the smallest value, taken over the unknowns being minimised
Lagrange multipliers.arg: the multipliers that make the dual objective largest (or smallest if written arg min)

Reading off the solution.alpha: the multiplier for example i: non-zero only for support vectors
